question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European Printing Presses and Education Centers]
options: Goa — First printing press in India established by the Jesuits (1556)
Serampore — Site of the Baptist Mission Press and college founded by Carey, Marshman, and Ward
Tranquebar — Danish Lutheran mission press established by Bartholomew Ziegenbalg (1712)
Calicut — Site of the first English translation of the Bhagavad Gita by Charles Wilkins
wrong_fact: Charles Wilkins translated the Bhagavad Gita into English in Bengal (Calcutta) in 1785 under the patronage of Warren Hastings, not in Calicut on the Malabar Coast.
explanation: The Jesuits brought the first printing press to Goa in 1556. Serampore in Bengal was the hub of missionary printing activities in the early 19th century. Ziegenbalg established a Tamil printing press in Danish Tranquebar in 1712. Wilkins' translation of the Gita was published in Calcutta, a milestone in orientalist scholarship.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Christian Missions and Architecture Style]
options: Basilica of Bom Jesus — Jesuit church in Goa housing the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier
San Thome Basilica — Neo-Gothic style church in Madras built over the tomb of St. Thomas
St. Francis Church — First European church in India built by the Portuguese in Cochin
Sardhana — Site of the Dutch Protestant Gothic Cathedral built by Begum Samru
wrong_fact: Begum Samru built the Basilica of Our Lady of Graces at Sardhana (near Meerut) as a Catholic church, designed by an Italian architect (Anthony Reghelini), not as a Dutch Protestant Cathedral.
explanation: The Basilica of Bom Jesus (Goa) is a UNESCO World Heritage site representing Baroque architecture. San Thome Basilica in Madras commemorates the Apostle St. Thomas. St. Francis Church in Cochin was built in 1503 where Vasco da Gama was initially buried. Sardhana's Basilica was constructed in 1822 under Begum Samru, who converted to Catholicism.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Botanical Gardens and Scientific Documentation]
options: Hortus Malabaricus — Compilation on medicinal plants of Kerala published by Dutch Governor Hendrik van Rheede
Sibpur (Calcutta) — Royal Botanic Garden founded by Robert Kyd in 1787 for acclimatizing plants
Daman and Diu — Centers for the introduction of New World crops like tobacco, cashew, and pineapple by the Portuguese
Pondicherry — Site where the first Sanskrit-French dictionary was compiled by Roberto de Nobili
wrong_fact: Roberto de Nobili was an Italian Jesuit missionary based in Madurai (under the Madurai Nayak kingdom), known for adopting Brahmanical customs. He did not compile a Sanskrit-French dictionary in Pondicherry.
explanation: Hortus Malabaricus was a landmark 12-volume botanical treatise published in Amsterdam. The Calcutta Botanic Garden was created to grow teak for ships and identify commercial crops. The Portuguese introduced crops from the Americas (chili, potato, tobacco, cashew, guava) to India via Daman, Diu, and Goa. Roberto de Nobili operated in Madurai in the early 17th century.
